subject: Term amendment: 90-day capacity runway + EU/APAC burst pools — onboarding & failover playbook
messages:
From: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@polylink.health>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophia Patel <sophia.patel@polylink.health>, procurement <procurement@polylink.health>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Term amendment request: capacity runway & EU/APAC pools

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the chat earlier. PolyLink's usage profile has spiked as we ramp a new caregiver-assist feature; we expect token throughput to increase roughly 3.5x for Q2-Q3 and need reserved capacity guarantees for EU and APAC regions during our renewal window. High level asks: 

- 90-day term amendment (short runway) to add: +96 A100-equivalent GPUs across two regional pools (EU, APAC) as reserved burst capacity.
- Throughput target: sustained 1.2M tokens/minute globally; p95 latency targets per region noted below.
- Failover expectations: automated cross-region fallback with warm standby in secondary region (APAC <-> US fallback acceptable).

Attached is our traffic forecast for the next 4 quarters and a short matrix of region-by-region latency tolerances. Can Redwood provide a term amendment + onboarding plan and an ops runbook for failover/on-call? Also copying procurement for commercial coordination.

Attachments: forecast_q1_q4.csv (csv), region_latency_tolerance.pdf (pdf)

Regards,
Arjun Mehta
Head of Platform
PolyLink Health

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@polylink.health>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Term amendment request: capacity runway & EU/APAC pools

Hi Arjun —

Appreciate the detail and for flagging the expected delta. We can definitely support a 90-day term amendment that provisions the regional reserved pools you describe as a temporary runway while your renewal/longer-term commitments finalize. Draft proposal (high level):

- Temporary amendment term: 90 days from effective date.
- Capacity: +96 A100-eq split as 48 GPUs in EU pool / 48 GPUs in APAC pool (reserved burst).
- Throughput guarantee: baseline 1.2M tokens/min across reserved capacity; we will provide per-region throughput shaping to keep p95 latency within agreed targets.
- Failover: cross-region warm standby with automated routing and prefix/KV cache seeding; planned RTO for cross-region fallback is 90s for session rehydration (detailed runbook to follow).
- Commercial: prorated committed fee for 90-day amendment + usage overage at standard dedicated surge rates.

I've attached a working capacity matrix (capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx) that maps expected utilization and suggested node counts per pool. Marissa will own the commercial redlines; Rishi will share the technical failover/runbook and on-call procedures.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to send draft amendment & DocuSign envelope.
2) Rishi to circulate the ops runbook and SLA excerpt for p95 latency.
3) Schedule a technical kickoff with PolyLink infra + Redwood infra next week (please share 2 slots).

Thanks — copying Marissa and Rishi.

—
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, North America
Redwood Inference

I've attached a first-pass amendment and the DocuSign packet (docusign_term-amendment.pdf). Key commercial points included:

From: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@polylink.health>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@polylink.health>, Sophia Patel <sophia.patel@polylink.health>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 08:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Contract amendment draft & next steps

Thanks Marissa — 

Two quick clarifications from our side before signature: 
1) Latency SLOs — we need p95 generation latency <= 220ms for EU and <= 260ms for APAC under the reserved capacity baseline. Can Redwood accept these as the contractual targets?
2) Failover behavior — during cross-region fallback, what is the user-visible session continuity expectation? If the KV cache needs rehydration, will sessions drop or will tokens continue with minimal context loss?

If you can confirm the SLO numbers and include a short excerpt in the amendment referencing the runbook behavior for session continuity, we can move quickly.

—
Arjun

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Arjun Mehta <arjun.mehta@polylink.health>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 02:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Contract amendment draft & next steps — technical runbook excerpt

Hi Arjun —

Thanks for the clarity. Short answers up front: yes, we can commit to the requested p95 latency targets under the reserved capacity baseline (EU <= 220ms, APAC <= 260ms) and we'll include those numbers in the SLA addendum.

Regarding failover/session continuity: 
- Primary behavior: automated routing to warm standby in secondary region. We pre-warm KV cache prefixes for active sessions during ramp windows; expected session continuity loss is minimal for stateless requests. For session-based contexts (long chats with large KV state), we provide a graceful degradation window: during the 90s RTO, the system will attempt to rehydrate session context from persisted prefix snapshots — in practice this causes an incremental latency spike for the first 5–10 tokens while the prefix is fetched.
- Operational details: on-call rotation will be staffed 24/7 during the 90-day runway at PolyLink's requested priority tier. On-call instructions & escalation matrix are attached in the runbook.

Quoted below is the short excerpt I recommend adding to section 7 of the amendment (ops runbook reference):

"Forwarded message:
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 02:18:00 -0800
Subject: Runbook excerpt — PolyLink 90-day runway

Runbook excerpt (summary):
- Warm standby seeding: 04:00 UTC pre-warm window for EU and 16:00 UTC pre-warm for APAC.
- RTO for cross-region fallback: 90s target.
- Session rehydration: prefix snapshot strategy; expected 5–10 token penalty on first response post-failover.
- On-call escalation: infra -> runtime -> SRE lead; pager escalation within 15 min if not acknowledged.

Attachments: sla_latency_targets.csv, runbook_oncall.md
"

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
